segments.text: So, how do we manage biological risk?
So, in order to manage biological risk, we have a biorisk management system ok.
So, in this module right, we will focus on the transgenic organisms and the risk associated
with transgenic organisms ok.
So, when we do the procedure of managing biological risk, we carry out the first thing we do
is risk assessment, we assess the risk associated with a particular organism.
After we assess the risk, we apply what are known as controls.
After we apply the controls, we measure what we is called the residual risk and if the
residual risk is acceptable, we proceed with the experiment.
For instance, I will give you a very simple example.
You have your car ok, the car by itself parked in the garage does not pose any risk.
However, when you take it out on the road, it starts becoming dynamic, then it begins
to pose risk to yourself, to the driver as well as to other users ok.
Now, the set of controls which we apply will mitigate the risk.
For instance, your seat belt is a control, your airbags are controls ok, your brake is
a control ok.
So, you have these controls which are actually engineering controls, they will protect you
and the surrounding environment from the risk posed by the car.
However, you also have what are known as administrative controls, your license is administrative control,
the laws which you follow are administrative controls ok.
These are, so you have different levels of controls, we will go into them and we will
formalize the different controls in the following slides.
So, when you have a risk, any risk, the formula for risk assessment is likelihood and consequence
ok.
Let us explore it with the analogy for the car.
You have a driver without a license driving on the road.
He is not aware of the laws and regulations, so he just drives, he only knows to drive
the car.
The likelihood of him meeting with an accident is very high, because he will jump red signals,
he will drive into pedestrians and the consequences of that action also very high ok.
Because if he kill, if he runs in the pedestrian, he will kill someone, if he runs into on
the vehicle, he will probably kill someone, so you have very high consequences.
Take the same example of a driver or an individual with a license to drive, so the
likelihood of that individual, he thinks someone is very low, because he was following
laws, he would not collide with a pedestrian or vehicle.
However, if he did collide, the consequences remain the same, you understood the general,
the likelihood is changes, but the consequence remains the same, the same driver hitting
a pedestrian, if he will basically cause the same level of injury.
So, in biological organisms, the same concept applies ok, so if you take a for example, if
you have a plant as in this case, you have a plant which is rice, which is open pollinated,
it will produce pollen and it will contaminate local land races.
So, if you have this plant release the pollen, you will have a impact on the economy, for
instance local farmers may say you have polluted our crops and then we can no longer sell them,
because the market says they are genetically modified, so there will be consequences for
the economy as well, so everything has to be measured in terms of likelihood and consequence.
So, if you can refer to this the table, you will see for example 1, 1 means the
low consequence, low likelihood ok and number 5, 5 is the high consequence and a high likelihood
ok. So, let us see this in terms of the pathogen like a human pathogen, a human pathogen which
can cause death for instance and which has no known cure ok. If you protect it in a lab,
the likelihood of it causing like a disease or a sickness is very low, because it is
contained in the lab. However, if that pathogen were to be released the consequence is very high,
because once it is released the consequence of accidental release or intentional release
is also very high ok. So, for instance if a terrorist were to steal that pathogen from
the lab hence propagate it throughout the system, the consequence will be high and if
it were to be accidentally released the consequence will be high as well. So,
everything every biological agent has to be looked in terms of the likelihood and
consequence, we have to consider that perspective ok.
So, once we go through this process of risk assessment, we will determine the level of
the risk. So, Sandia national labs developed this procedure which is known as AMP. So,
they assess the risk, they mitigate the risk and then they assess the performance of
their management system. So, how do we determine the level of risk associated with an experiment
with a particular pathogen ok. When we have a pathogen right in the lab it poses no risk,
it is there in the lab it poses no risk, but the process of carrying out an experiment with it
is the one which poses the risk. For instance we have a genetically modified seed in the lab,
it is not going to pose any risk. However, when there is a researcher you take it out from the lab,
you plant it in a greenhouse and then you get a plant and you have pollen then level of risk
increases the degree of risk basically increases. So, these are things which you need to take into
account when you do risk assessment. For instance if you are a researcher is saying
I am working with genetically modified seeds, the next question you will ask him what are
going to do with the seeds. For instance he says oh I am just going to extract DNA from the seeds.
So, the risk is very low, likelihood and consequence of that material going out of
the seed and going into under plant is very low ok. So, that is a different aspect which
you need to look into. However, if he says I am going to plant this seed and I am going to
harvest the pollen and then check for the DNA or the genetically modified material in the pollen,
then your risk increases. So, both the likelihood and consequence also increase.
So, these are some of the questions which we ask researchers. So, there is no general set
of question, you have to develop a specific risk assessment for a specific procedure or
a specific experiment. So, when since we will ask the researcher has the organism been
genetically modified. So, is there any experimental evidence which says that
this modification is dangerous. However, if it is a new case you do not know then you
this question will be a gray area. So, what is a lethal dose instead some of the genes may have
a lethal dose when you feed them in certain concentration to animal in animal test they
may have proven to be lethal in that case you need to take precautions. So,
these are the various questions which you ask. So, one of them is training number 6 is training.
So, has the researcher been received training in terms of handling the material and you have
to ask if the project will be carried out under containment. So, in case in the event that you
are involved in basically in a management situation you need to develop this kind of
questionnaires to assess the risk. So, then you then categorize them into the risk group in which
case you need to refer to your NIH guideline you classify them into the risk group. So,
once you have identified the risk group and you have identified all the assessment you
are carried out a risk assessment you need to mitigate or reduce the risk. So,
risk assessment is asking questions and is passive you ask questions just keep asking risk
mitigation is where you carry out the process of limiting the risk. So,
there is a specific procedure which you need to follow. This slide actually pertains the
hierarchy of controls. The hierarchy is staggered level of risk mitigation. The first level is
elimination for instance if you carried out a risk assessment and then you determine that
the risk is too great and you do not have the personnel you do not have the training
you do not have the facilities you do not have the equipment you do what is known as an
elimination. Elimination means you do not carry out the experiment you inform the
researcher saying that this experiment is too risky please do not carry it carry out this
experiment. The second one is substitution you have a plant for instance which is posing a risk
for instance you have genetically modified a plant with a pathogenic for instance the
pathogenic virus. You have you can suggest to the researcher to carry out substitution.
Substitution means you carry out an experiment however you mutate the gene to reduce the level
of pathogenicity or you mutate the virus you attenuate the virus so that the level of
risk is reduced. So, that is from the substitution. The third control is the
engineering control now this is the expensive control because it involves the facility itself
so the air conditioning system that keep our filters filtration system the air locks okay
the negative air flow all these are engineering controls. So, when your engineering controls
have been taken care of you have your administrative control. Administrative
controls is your organizational structure and your SOPs all your SOPs your measures your
records your documents in administrative controls and the last line of defense is basically the
personal protective equipment which are your gloves your suits your respirators okay and
the SOP associated with usage of these equipment. For instance you may have a perfect respirator
a perfect mask a perfect covering for your body to protect yourself. However, if you do not know
how to use it you will basically it is loses its purpose that is why you have administrative
controls. So, with every equipment with every procedure in the lab there is a administrative
control they all these controls work in tandem. So, elimination and substitution if you do if
your risk assessment indicates that you have to eliminate a substitute you have to inform
the researcher. So, the other ones are basically part of the physical structure the engineering
controls okay. So, elimination as I told you is basically stopping all research however there
are consequences for this if you stopped all your research you will basically not have any
progress okay you would not know. So, you need to give a certain level of freedom and then you
need to apply containment that is why we have the expensive containment facilities because we
want to do research with pathogens. However, we are taking all the measures to contain the
usage or the release of those pathogens. Substitution basically involves reducing the
level of risk by modifying the biological process. So, one perfect example of substitution
will be virus which is used for vaccination is attenuated attenuated is weakened. So,
it cannot propagate so it can elicit a immune response but cannot propagate the engineering
controls pertain to all your filters your physical barriers and your air flow.
So, in a containment facility the primary barrier is air flow you know you reverse the
air flow. So, for example, you have a pathogen in this room most offices for
example this room is basically having a positive pressure. So, the air comes in through the
air conditioning system when you open the door there will be air flowing out. So,
anything which is in this room will basically exit. So, that is designed for our comfort.
So, you get oxygen fresh oxygen coming in. In the case of containment facility you have
the reverse. So, when you open the door you will actually have air rushing in. So,
the air rushes in goes to the system is passed through several HEPA filters and is pumped out.
So, that is the reverse that is the difference between a conventional air flow and a directional
air flow. Then you have your administrative controls which is all your training the SOPs,
the records all categorized as administrative controls. And finally, you have your personal
protective equipment. So, this is called the last line of defense for instance in Africa you
have the Ebola virus they do not have transgenic facilities for protection they do not have
containment facilities. However, they have the PPEs the personal protective equipment. So, you anywhere
personal protective equipment as I said earlier you need to follow the SOP. For instance if you
have some kind of virus on your glove and you did not doff your glove properly you did not take
it off there is a likelihood that you will transfer the virus back onto your skin. And that
will get a higher concentration because you took it for granted that you are working with PPE and
you can touch everything. So, it increases your level of risk of exposure. Finally, you have
performance assessment usually in the case of plants we have what is known as Sentinel Plant.
For instance when you do a risk assessment for crops you can suggest to the researcher
please ensure that you build your facility within a 1 kilometer radius of any rice field.
So, it has to be outside. So, any rice crops or any local farmers crops have to be
growing beyond 1 kilometer. So, how do you determine is 1 kilometer you have you did
certain test prior to that you determine the flow of the air. So, you should be aware of
all these things before you suggest measures for mitigation. So, one of the measures which
has been practiced globally for determination of performance of your facility is what is known
as sentinel crops. The concept of sentinel is like this you have your facility your containment
facility and you have taken all the measures to protect the release of pollen. Now, what you do
is you plant local varieties of rice around that facility when since you are working with
transgenic rice you plant local varieties of rice every 50 meters in your surrounded facility.
At the end of each cropping cycle when you harvest your crop you also harvest the seed
from that crop. You then extract the DNA and you do a amplification or polymerase chain reaction
of a specific gene which is transgenic and you test for the presence of that
gene. These are known as the sentinel plants. So, sentinel plants are used for assessment of your
facilities ability to contain risk. So, that is called performance assessment. So, this is the
concept. So, you have a genetically modified plant and you have a area around in which you
cultivate local land races. So, the word local land races is plants which are found in that
region. For instance if I if you have a variety of rice which is endemic to this particular part
of the world then I transferred it to the lab I genetically modified it and then I propagated
as a hybrid or a genetically modified variety. When I grow these with the local plants the
local plants are referred to as local land races. So, ideally I should have enabled basically
created a sterile variant. So, the pollen is not produced and does not propagate into local
plants. Even if it is produced it will be sterile it would not impact local plants.
So, the last part of this module we focus on facility design.
